Join the leading maritime news network On 24 November 2026, Windcat signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for the second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) in the Innovation Series. The contract follows the order for the first vessel , with an option for five more, signed in November last year. Sound basis The MP-ASV is an entirely new type of vessel designed to support operations in the offshore energy industry . Its design draws heavily on Damen’s experience in the design and construction of Commissioning Services Operations Vessels (CSOVs). This includes the Elevation Series CSOVs, developed together by Damen and Windcat. The first vessel in the Elevation Series, Windcat Rotterdam , was presented with the KNVTS Ship of the Year Award at this year’s Maritime Awards Gala. The MP-ASV takes the proven capabilities of the Elevation Series CSOVs and builds on them further. Extended capabilities The MP-ASVs build on these capabilities in a number of ways, including with their 102 x 20 metre hull and its 750m 2 deck space. The MP-ASV is able to assist and operate in all offshore energy markets, including cable repair, flotel functions, offshore wind and ROV assistance. Additionally, the vessel is fitted with 111 cabins, allowing up to 190 persons on board. The vessel features an offshore crane which can be used as a 150-tonne subsea crane, or as a 15-tonne 3D motion-compensated crane. The vessel can also be fitted with remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). The vessels are being equipped with a DP2+ system holding DNV CBS and CBT class notations, which cover a wider scope of redundant closed bus-ties system arrangements, for enhanced fault tolerance. The DP system features additional tunnel thrusters fore and aft to provide increased redundancy for safe operations in remote offshore locations. Access is via a 3D motion-compensated gangway with two exchangeable tips, one for short connections used in the wind industry and one capable of long continuous connections. Prepared for efficiency The MP-ASVs will be outfitted with a battery system to enable peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing. This will enable highly efficient operations, for example when in DP mode. Like the Windcat CSOVs, a key feature of the Innovation Series vessels is the integration of low-carbon fuels . Hence a dual fuel hydrogen auxiliary genset is installed, and the three main generator sets are of the next generation Evolve generator sets from ABC, which allow for a range of low-emission possibilities. These engines can operate on liquid fuels such as biodiesel and HVO, on dual fuel with pilot injection of liquid fuel, or on 100% gas using spark ignition. High offshore comfort level The design of the vessel is also highly focused on comfort for the up to 190 personnel onboard. Measures include well-thought-out routing, use of high-quality materials and aesthetically appealing accommodation. The aim is to make crew and personnel feel at home during extended periods of up to 150 days offshore, due to her extended fuel capacity. Strength-to-strength Damen Sales Director Joost van der Weiden says, “We are delighted to receive this second MP-ASV order from Windcat. The cooperation that began with our development of the Elevation Series continues to grow in strength. With the Innovation Series we mutually have developed a vessel that will further enhance Windcat’s capabilities to support its clients in the offshore energy industry in the years ahead.” Windcat Managing Director Willem van der Wel says: “The decision to order a second MP-ASV reflects our confidence in this new vessel concept and our ambition to further strengthen our position in the offshore energy market. By combining the capabilities of a multi-purpose support vessel with high-quality offshore accommodation, we are creating a versatile solution that responds to the evolving needs of our customers. The Shenzhen-listed company’s shipping arm, Shenzhen Energy Transportation, has named the Guangzhou-based yard as the winning bidder for the vessel, which will replace its ageing 1997-built, 69,000 dwt panamax Jia Chang (pictured). The award follows an investment decision in June, when Shenzhen Energy approved a budget of RMB309.68m ($46.5m) for the newbuilding as part of efforts to modernise its coal transportation fleet. The vessel will be designed to run on conventional marine fuels, with provision for a future conversion to methanol propulsion. According to the group’s earlier stock exchange disclosure, the project will be financed through RMB64m in internal funds, with the remainder covered by external financing. Shenzhen Energy Transportation operates six panamax bulk carriers totalling around 450,000 dwt, transporting coal to the group’s power plants while also serving the international dry bulk market. Its trading activities cover routes linking China with Australia, the Americas, Africa and Southeast Asia. articles.title: Hong Kong shipowners hail shipping tax overhaul
articles.summary: The Hong Kong Shipowners Association (HKSOA) has welcomed a package of tax reforms aimed at attracting more shipping and commodity trading businesses to the city, including a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity traders. articles.body: Greater China Operations Regulatory Hong Kong shipowners hail shipping tax overhaul Adis Ajdin November 25, 2026 0 306 1 minute read The Hong Kong Shipowners Association (HKSOA) has welcomed a package of tax reforms aimed at attracting more shipping and commodity trading businesses to the city, including a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity traders. The measures, which returned to the Legislative Council for consideration on Wednesday, would reduce the profits tax rate on qualifying commodity trading activities from 16.5% to 8.25%, while expanding existing concessions for ship leasing, shipmanagement, ship agency and broking businesses. The legislation also introduces an optional 15% tax rate for qualifying shipping companies and commodity traders covered by the OECD’s global minimum tax rules, allowing them to simplify compliance under the BEPS 2.0 framework. For ship lessors, the changes include broader deductions for vessel acquisition costs and financing expenses, alongside greater flexibility in leasing arrangements. The commodity trading concession is designed to bring more trading houses to Hong Kong and generate additional demand for local shipping services. Under the proposed framework, eligible traders must meet minimum business turnover and local operating requirements, including conditions linking expenditure on maritime services to Hong Kong-based providers. The government has previously estimated that the concessions could generate HK$4.6bn ($590m) in economic benefits by encouraging commodity traders to establish or expand their operations in the city. HKSOA chairman Richard Hext said the measures reflected cooperation between the government, legislators and the shipping industry. “The shipping sector is a highly competitive industry, requiring the support of many community stakeholders, including the government and legislators,” Hext said. “The new tax measures are an excellent example of public-private partnership. Each and every such initiative adds to Hong Kong’s attraction as a global maritime capital.” The association, which represents more than 200 shipping and maritime-related businesses, said it would work with the Inland Revenue Department to help the industry adapt to the new requirements. Hong Kong has been offering preferential tax treatment to qualifying ship lessors since 2020, extending concessions to ship leasing managers and other commercial maritime service providers in subsequent years. The latest reforms form part of the government’s wider effort to strengthen the city’s role as a maritime finance, shipping and commodity trading centre. articles.title: Petronas Names ‘World's First’ Nearshore FLNG Facility
articles.summary: Petronas has officially named its third floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility, PFLNG TIGA, at Samsung Heavy Industries' shipyard in South Korea, ahead of its planned deployment to Malaysia and start-up in the third quarter of 2027.Described…
articles.body: Petronas Names ‘World's First’ Nearshore FLNG Facility Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Petronas) Petronas has officially named its third floating liquefied natural gas (FLNG) facility, PFLNG TIGA, at Samsung Heavy Industries' shipyard in South Korea, ahead of its planned deployment to Malaysia and start-up in the third quarter of 2027. Described by Petronas as the world's first nearshore FLNG facility, PFLNG TIGA is currently under construction at the shipyard on Geoje Island and will be deployed to Sipitang, Sabah, Malaysia. The facility is designed to produce 2 million tonnes of LNG annually and measures 281 metres in length, 64 metres in width and 32 metres in depth. PFLNG TIGA will become the third floating LNG facility developed by Petronas , expanding its portfolio of facilities designed for shallow-water, deepwater and nearshore environments. The new facility is intended to support the development and commercialisation of gas resources while strengthening Malaysia's LNG supply capabilities. Petronas said the addition would provide greater flexibility in bringing gas resources to market and meeting regional and international demand. The company has been active in the LNG industry for more than four decades, with PFLNG TIGA representing another addition to its integrated LNG portfolio.

Neda currently manages nine tankers, comprising five VLCCs and four aframaxes, alongside 16 dry bulk carriers. The deals follow MPCC’s $340m swoop for four modern 7,000 teu containerships in June, each backed by a three-year charter to a major liner operator. MPCC said on Wednesday that the takeover of the quartet had been pushed back, resulting in a reduction in the purchase price. The company’s contracted revenue backlog stands at $2.2bn, with 90% of available days covered for next year, 66% for 2028 and 42% for 2029. articles.body: Oil Falls as Supply Glut Concerns Overshadow Hormuz Shipping Risks Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 © Miha Creative / Adobe Stock Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East. Brent crude futures LCOc1 declined 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 slipped 62 cents, or 0.8%, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday. "Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage. On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery ‌and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast ‌that ⁠also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude. A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said. US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. API/S Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average. "Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said. Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya. "However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said. A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media. On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday. (Reuters - Reporting by Anna Hirtenstein in London. Additional reporting by Jeslyn Lerh in Singapore and Yuka Obayashi in Tokyo; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus)

articles.body: Windcat Expands Offshore Fleet with Second Damen Multi-Purpose Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Windcat) Windcat has signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for a second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) under its Innovation Series, expanding its planned fleet of vessels designed for offshore energy operations. The agreement, signed on November 24, follows Windcat's initial order in November 2025 for the first vessel in the series, which included an option for five additional units. The new MP-ASV design builds on the companies' earlier collaboration on the Elevation Series commissioning service operations vessels (CSOVs), incorporating additional capabilities for offshore wind, subsea cable repair, offshore accommodation and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) support. The vessels will measure 102 meters in length and 20 meters in width, with approximately 750 square meters of deck space and 111 cabins accommodating up to 190 personnel. Each MP-ASV will feature an offshore crane capable of operating as a 150-tonne subsea crane or a 15-tonne three-dimensional motion-compensated crane, alongside provisions for ROV installation. Personnel transfers will be supported by a 3D motion-compensated gangway with interchangeable tips designed for short connections in offshore wind operations and longer continuous connections. The vessels will also feature a DP2+ dynamic positioning system with DNV CBS and CBT class notations, incorporating additional bow and stern tunnel thrusters to improve redundancy during offshore operations. The propulsion and power arrangement will include a battery system for peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing, together with a dual-fuel hydrogen auxiliary generator. Three main generator sets supplied by ABC will feature its Evolve technology, designed to accommodate different fuel options, including biodiesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), dual-fuel operation and gas. The MP-ASVs are designed for extended offshore deployments of up to 150 days, supported by increased fuel capacity and accommodation facilities intended for prolonged stays at sea. The Innovation Series builds on Damen and Windcat's Elevation Series partnership, which includes the Windcat Rotterdam, named KNVTS Ship of the Year at the 2026 Maritime Awards Gala.

The New York- and Athens-listed owner revealed in a US securities filing that it had agreed to offload the Japanese-built, 87,000 dwt Marina , with the vessel set to change hands in January next year. The buyer has not been disclosed. The Cyprus-flagged 2006-built bulker has been part of the Safe Bulkers fleet since its early years. The vessel had a carrying value of around $9.3m at the end of September. The latest fleet exit marks the fourth vessel sale agreed by Safe Bulkers this year, taking the combined gross value of the disposals to around $77.6m. In February, the company agreed to sell the 2012-built capesize Michalis H for $35.2m, followed in May by deals to offload the 2008-built kamsarmax Pedhoulas Commander and the 2006-built post-panamax Xenia . Safe Bulkers has been balancing the secondhand sales with investment in new tonnage, having raised €80.4m ($93.5m) through a private placement in September to support its fleet expansion. As of November 20, the owner controlled 46 bulkers totalling around 4.53m dwt, with an average age of 9.9 years. The company’s orderbook comprises seven kamsarmaxes and one capesize scheduled for delivery between 2027 and 2029. articles.summary: Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting…
articles.body: NextGeo Gets $12.7M Offshore Survey Job for Spain-France Hydrogen Link Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting Spain and France. The contract covers an integrated survey campaign along an approximately 366-kilometre offshore corridor between Barcelona, Spain, and Fos-sur-Mer, France. The scope includes geophysical, geotechnical and UXO surveys, grab sampling, remotely operated vehicle (ROV) inspections and surveys of crossings with existing subsea infrastructure. The data collected will be used to characterise seabed and sub-seabed conditions to support the planning and design of the future pipeline. NextGeo will deploy two dedicated vessels for the offshore operations, which are expected to begin by the end of 2026. The campaign is currently scheduled for completion between the end of the second quarter and the beginning of the third quarter of 2027, depending on any additional work requested during execution. The BarMar pipeline forms part of H2med, a cross-border initiative designed to connect hydrogen networks in the Iberian Peninsula with northwestern Europe. The project is being developed by BarMar S.A.S., whose shareholders are NaTran, Enagás and Teréga. H2med is included on the European Union's list of Projects of Common Interest, with BarMar providing the planned maritime hydrogen transport connection between Spain and France. The award marks NextGeo's first contract with BarMar, expanding its offshore survey activities into hydrogen infrastructure development.

Vantris, formerly known as Sapura Energy, has been rebuilding its offshore contracting business following a major financial restructuring completed in 2025. The company exited Bursa Malaysia’s financially distressed PN17 classification in June after more than four years, allowing it to concentrate on replenishing its orderbook and securing work across its core engineering, construction and drilling businesses. The company’s offshore energy division will carry out marine construction work associated with the 50 km offshore section of the natural gas pipeline in British Columbia. The scope includes seabed preparation, trenching, pipeline stabilisation, backfilling, and span rectification, as well as landfall construction at Nass Bay, Iceberg Bay, Nasoga Gulf, and Wil Milit. Preparatory work is scheduled to begin in 2027, followed by two offshore installation campaigns. NW Infrastructure, a joint venture between Western LNG and the Nisga’a Nation, is developing the pipeline to transport natural gas from northeastern British Columbia to the planned Ksi Lisims LNG export facility on Pearse Island. Splash reported in July that Allseas secured the main offshore installation contract from Western LNG for approximately 50 km of 36-inch and 48-inch pipelines. Allseas intends to deploy its pipelay vessels Solitaire and Sandpiper for installation work in water depths of up to 450 metres, with offshore pipelaying scheduled for 2029. The Ksi Lisims LNG development is a proposed floating LNG export facility with an annual production capacity of 12m tonnes. The project is being jointly developed by the Nisga’a Nation, Rockies LNG, and Western LNG, targeting exports to markets across the Pacific basin, primarily in Asia. Join the leading maritime news network Two established naval architecture and marine engineering firms become 100% employee owned, carrying forward the vision and values of their founders. Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) and The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI) are proud to announce that both companies are now 100% employee owned through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), marking an important milestone for the two naval architecture and marine engineering firms. For Gregory W. Beers, P.E., and Cory C. Wood, who founded BHGI in 1995 and later established TSGI in 2010, the transition represents the continuation of a vision that began more than three decades ago: to build the most well-respected naval architecture and marine engineering firms in the industry. Gregory and Cory have spent decades building BHGI and TSGI with a vision that extends well beyond their own leadership. Through careful planning, the development of strong management teams, and a continued investment in their employees, they have positioned both firms to become multigenerational leaders in the naval architecture and marine engineering industry. The transition to employee ownership is a significant step in securing that future, ensuring that the companies they founded continue to grow and succeed for generations to come. While ownership has changed, both firms will continue operating much as they have for years. Gregory and Cory will remain at the forefront of both companies, providing leadership and direction alongside their established management teams. Clients can continue to expect the same level of service and technical expertise from the employees they’ve come to know and trust over the years. BHGI’s History BHGI traces its origins back to 1993, when Gregory and Cory, along with Andy Tyska of Bristol Marine and another fellow student at the University of Michigan Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Department set out to design a passenger vessel while still in school. Their first design, the STAR OF SAUGATUCK II , marked an early milestone for the firm and is still operating on the Kalamazoo River in Southwest Michigan. Building on that early initiative, the group formally incorporated BHGI in 1995, and the firm has continued to grow in Bristol, Rhode Island, ever since. Over the years, BHGI has developed into a close-knit team of 19, maintaining a hands-on, collaborative working environment. Today, the engineering team is led by Daniel P. Eling, P.E. For more than three decades, BHGI has been guided by a set of core values established early on by Greg and Cory. Those values continue to shape the firm’s work today and center on technical excellence, attention to detail, a strong focus on clients, engineering ethics, professionalism, and responsibility. TSGI’s History In 2010, Gregory and Cory formed The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI), a sister company to BHGI located in Houston, Texas. The company was established when Gregory and Cory purchased the assets of Shearer & Assoc., Inc. from Edward L. Shearer, P.E., its founder and president. The three had heard of one another through industry connections and eventually met at a SNAME convention. That encounter led to further discussions, and ultimately the formation of TSGI. The “Shearer” name has long been associated with the inland marine industry, reflecting both Ed’s contributions to naval architecture and his family’s multigenerational barge line. When TSGI was established, it brought together Ed’s years of experience at Shearer & Associates, Inc. and the naval architecture and marine engineering expertise Gregory and Cory had developed at BHGI. Ed remains involved as a Principal Naval Architect. Today, TSGI provides marine engineering services to clients in the inland and offshore marine industries. The firm offers many of the same services as BHGI, along with additional services suited to its Houston location, including marine surveying and OSHA-compliant maritime gear certification support. As TSGI continued to grow, Joshua S. Sebastian, P.E., joined the firm in 2013, bringing five years of engineering experience at BHGI, along with his nine-year background as an officer in the U.S. Coast Guard. He relocated to Texas to serve as Engineering Manager, as part of Gregory and Cory’s plan to build TSGI with the same technical and cultural approach used at BHGI. In 2022, Joshua stepped into the role of Vice President – Operations, with Senior Naval Architect Harrison C. Brann, P.E., stepping into the role of Engineering Manager. Over 15 years, TSGI has grown into another close-knit team of 19. Under Joshua and Harrison’s leadership, TSGI has continued to grow while maintaining the same approach and core principles established at BHGI. Today, the firm remains dedicated to serving vessels that operate on the inland waterways and continuing the tradition established by its namesake. Leadership and Employee Ownership With the ESOP now in place, Gregory will serve as Chairman and President, Cory as Vice Chairman, and Joshua as Vice President of both BHGI and TSGI. The engineering teams will continue under the direction of Daniel at BHGI and Harrison at TSGI, both as Engineering Managers. What began as a design effort in a college house has grown into two established firms, each built in a steady and deliberate way. Over the years, Gregory and Cory have built management teams that allow BHGI and TSGI to grow without losing sight of the values on which they were founded. Now, with ownership in the hands of their employees, both firms will continue the work they were built to do, guided by the same commitment to their clients, their profession, and a shared belief that their purpose is to create. To mark the transition to employee ownership, BHGI and TSGI recognized employees who were with the firms at the time as “Plank Owners,” a nautical term traditionally used for members of a vessel’s commissioning crew. Each employee received a commemorative “Built to Last” challenge coin featuring the “Plank Owner” designation. Both offices also have permanent “Plank Owner” plaques on display, recognizing these employees and their place in the companies’ history. For BHGI and TSGI, employee ownership is another part of what it means to be built to last. About BHGI Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) is a naval architecture and marine engineering firm located in Bristol, Rhode Island. Founded in 1995, BHGI provides vessel design, engineering, and consulting services to commercial and government clients throughout the marine industry. To learn more, you can visit our website: http://bristolharborgroup.com . About TSGI The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI) is a naval architecture and marine engineering firm located in Houston, Texas. Established in 2010, TSGI provides naval architecture, marine engineering, marine surveying, and related consulting services to clients in the inland and offshore marine industries. articles.title: Maersk and ONE Eye Landmark Global North-South Shipping Alliance
articles.summary: The formation of container shipping’s first global liner alliance covering the north-south trades appears to be taking shape, The Loadstar has learned.

Join the leading maritime news network Containers are seen on the Maersk's Triple-E giant container ship Majestic Maersk, one of the world's largest container ships, next to cranes at the APM Terminals in the port of Algeciras, Spain January 20, 2023. REUTERS/Jon Nazca/File Photo By Nils Roche (The Loadstar) – The formation of container shipping’s first global liner alliance covering the north-south trades appears to be taking shape, The Loadstar has learned. Container lines have traditionally treated the north-south trades as a set of separate marriages, on the assumption that the right partner depends on the trade. However, according to sources in Asia, Maersk and Ocean Network Express (ONE) are working to develop a vessel-sharing agreement (VSA) covering the trades globally, rather than lane by lane. The Loadstar has approached both carriers for comment but has yet to receive a formal response, and the form the VDSA would take is unclear. Nonetheless, if confirmed it would be the first VSA of its kind – and its logic rests on ONE’s fleet, according to our provisional analysis below. Their respective groupings, the Gemini Cooperation for Maersk and Premier Alliance for ONE, stop at east-west trades, while north-south has remained a patchwork of classic VSAs, where each carrier’s slots follow the ships it provides, and an agreement rarely covers more than two or three services. Why not Hapag-Lloyd? The obvious choice of partner for Maersk would be Hapag-Lloyd, its Gemini compatriot – but two things rule it out. The first is that CSAV owns 30% of it and sits in the shareholder pact that controls more than 70% of the carrier, so combining West Coast South America networks would join two incumbents serving the same Chilean and Peruvian exporters. In that context, it is worth noting that Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd do not cooperate on any of their respective Asia-WC South America services – according to Xeneta’s eeSea liner database, Maersk operates two standalone strings, the AC1 and AC3, while Hapag-Lloyd’s three offerings are run in cooperation with MSC, HMM, and ONE. Secondly, Hapag-Lloyd has relatively few ships coming – its orderbook is 19% of its fleet, the lowest of the eight largest carriers, on trades where Far East–Latin America capacity grew 14% in a year. ONE poses fewer of those problems. On Far East–WC South America, for example, Linerlytica puts Maersk at 16.1% of weekly capacity and ONE at 9%; together a quarter of the trade, ahead of CMA CGM and MSC, from two carriers whose customers overlap less. The ships are the point ONE has the fleet those trades are moving towards. Alphaliner puts 36% of its operated capacity in ships of 10,000–15,100 teu, against 14% at Maersk. Of the 55 ships ONE has on order, 29 – representing 60% of the total 647,000 teu expected – fall in the same bracket. Linerlytica puts the average ship on Far East–Latin America already at 10,032 teu. However, only 10 of ONE’s 62 ships in that class currently work Latin American routes. Under the classic formula, ships buy slots, so tonnage converts directly into share. A global partner gives ONE’s newbuilds work without ONE building Latin American and African franchises alone. Maersk, whose next order according to Linerlytica is for 24,000 teu ships, would thus get mid-size capacity without ordering it. What it will probably look like “Global” may describe the scope more than the mechanics. North-south shippers pay for direct calls, Brazil reserves feeder legs for Brazilian-flag operators, and Mexico’s ports do little relay business. That points to core loops on one carrier’s ships where its fleet fits, and shared loops where the ship mix demands it, rather than a Gemini-style hub network. The obstacles are real. Hapag-Lloyd sits alongside ONE in several of these consortia, so the deal means reordering them with Maersk’s own Gemini partner, and a quarter of Asia–WC South America capacity will interest regulators in Chile and Peru. And similar disentanglements will be necessary on other north-south trades: for example, Maersk continues to cooperate with CMA CGM on Asia-West Africa services. And although there were rumours that that cooperation might be coming to an end, they have subsided for now. The quay question… …will be where ONE’s 13,724 teu newbuilds are deployed in 2027. The industry has assumed north-south partners must be chosen trade by trade. A Maersk–ONE framework tests a different premise: that the scarce input is the right ship, and a carrier holding them can be a partner almost everywhere.
